title_en: Bai Guanghua v. Tianjin Labor Reeducation Management Committee — dispute over labor reeducation decision
ruling_gist_en: Article 12, paragraph 2 of the Trial Measures for Reeducation through Labor stipulates: "Where a person who has been decided to be reeducated through labor disagrees with the principal facts, the approving authority shall organize a review." The term "review" here should be understood as the original approving authority conducting a re-examination of the decision on reeducation through labor, and shall not be understood or regarded as administrative reconsideration. The current laws and regulations of our country do not require administrative litigation cases regarding disagreement with reeducation through labor decisions to undergo a mandatory preliminary procedure of administrative reconsideration. A party who disagrees with a decision on reeducation through labor has the right, in accordance with the provisions of the Administrative Reconsideration Law, to freely choose either to apply for administrative reconsideration or to directly file an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court.

full_text_en:
Bai Guanghua v. Tianjin Reeducation-through-Labor Management Committee — dispute over reeducation-through-labor decision

Ruling Summary

Article 12(2) of the Interim Measures on Reeducation-through-Labor provides: "If a person determined to be subject to reeducation-through-labor disagrees with the main facts, the approving authority shall organize a review." The term "review" as used herein shall be understood as the original approving authority's reexamination of the reeducation-through-labor decision, and shall not be construed or deemed as administrative reconsideration. Current laws and regulations of China do not provide that administrative litigation cases disputing a reeducation-through-labor decision must go through administrative reconsideration as a prerequisite procedure. A party who disagrees with a reeducation-through-labor decision has the right, in accordance with the Administrative Reconsideration Law, to freely choose either to apply for administrative reconsideration or to directly file an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court.

Plaintiff: Bai Guanghua, male, 44 years old, Hui ethnicity, unemployed, residing at Xibeijiao Xinchun Huayuan, Hongqiao District, Tianjin.

Defendant: Tianjin Reeducation-through-Labor Management Committee, domiciled at Tangshan Road, Heping District, Tianjin.

Legal Representative: Song Pingshun, Chairman of the Committee.

Plaintiff Bai Guanghua, disagreeing with the reeducation-through-labor decision made by the Defendant Tianjin Reeducation-through-Labor Management Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Labor Management Committee"), filed an administrative lawsuit with the Tianjin No. 1 Intermediate People's Court.

Plaintiff Bai Guanghua alleged: On December 30, 2004, the Defendant Labor Management Committee, on the ground that the Plaintiff had disturbed social order, made Jinlaojiaoshen (2005) No. 42 "Decision on Reeducation-through-Labor", deciding to subject the Plaintiff to reeducation-through-labor for one year and six months. The labor reeducation decision made by the Defendant lacks factual basis, does not meet the scope and conditions prescribed by laws and regulations on reeducation-through-labor, clearly misapplies the law, and the procedure is also unlawful. The Plaintiff requests the court to revoke the specific administrative act made by the Defendant in accordance with law.

Defendant Labor Management Committee argued: Article 12(2) of the Interim Measures on Reeducation-through-Labor provides: "If a person determined to be subject to reeducation-through-labor disagrees with the main facts, the approving authority shall organize a review." Article 37(2) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC provides: "Where laws or regulations provide that a party shall first apply to an administrative organ for reconsideration and may file a lawsuit with the People's Court only if he is dissatisfied with the reconsideration decision, such provisions shall be followed." Pursuant to the above provisions, Plaintiff Bai Guanghua, if dissatisfied with the reeducation-through-labor decision made by the Defendant, should first apply for reconsideration with the Defendant's approving authority within the prescribed time limit, and may file an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court only if dissatisfied with the reconsideration decision. Now, the Plaintiff directly filed an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court without going through administrative reconsideration; therefore, the People's Court should not accept the case. The Defendant requests the court to rule to dismiss the Plaintiff's complaint.

The Tianjin No. 1 Intermediate People's Court found the following facts upon trial:

On December 30, 2004, the Labor Management Committee, pursuant to Article 1 of the "State Council Notice on Unifying the Two Measures of Compulsory Labor and Shelter and Investigation into Reeducation-through-Labor", on the ground that Plaintiff Bai Guanghua had disturbed social order, made Jinlaojiaoshen (2005) No. 42 "Decision on Reeducation-through-Labor", deciding to subject Bai Guanghua to reeducation-through-labor for one year and six months. Bai Guanghua, dissatisfied with this decision, filed an administrative lawsuit with the Tianjin No. 1 Intermediate People's Court. Prior to this, Bai Guanghua had not applied for administrative reconsideration of this decision.

The focus of the dispute in this case is: whether the People's Court should accept the case when Plaintiff Bai Guanghua, dissatisfied with the reeducation-through-labor decision made by the Defendant Labor Management Committee, directly files an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court without going through the administrative reconsideration procedure.

The Tianjin No. 1 Intermediate People's Court held at first instance:

Plaintiff Bai Guanghua, dissatisfied with the "Decision on Reeducation-through-Labor" made by the Defendant Labor Management Committee, should, in accordance with Article 9 of the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the PRC, first file an application for administrative reconsideration with the approving authority within 60 days from the date of learning of the specific administrative act. Only if dissatisfied with the reconsideration decision may he file a lawsuit with the People's Court. However, the Plaintiff, after receiving the reeducation-through-labor decision, did not apply for administrative reconsideration but directly filed a lawsuit with the court on May 30, 2005, which does not comply with the provisions of Article 12(2) of Document Guofa (1982) No. 17, the Interim Measures on Reeducation-through-Labor, and therefore should not be accepted.

Accordingly, the Tianjin No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 37(2) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 44(11) of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, ruled to dismiss the complaint of Plaintiff Bai Guanghua.

Bai Guanghua, dissatisfied with the first-instance ruling, filed an appeal with the Tianjin High People's Court, requesting to set aside the original ruling and to revoke the Jinlaojiaoshen (2005) No. 42 "Decision on Reeducation-through-Labor" made by the Appellee Labor Management Committee, with litigation costs borne by the Appellee. His main reasons were: 1. The "review" stipulated in Article 12(2) of the Interim Measures on Reeducation-through-Labor is not "administrative reconsideration." Article 9 of the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the PRC provides: Citizens, legal persons, or other organizations that believe a specific administrative act has infringed their lawful rights and interests may file an application for administrative reconsideration. However, the first-instance ruling erroneously determined that the Appellant "shall" first apply for administrative reconsideration with the approving authority and may not directly file a lawsuit with the People's Court, which constitutes an error in the application of law. 2. Article 37 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC provides: "In the case of an administrative case that falls within the scope of acceptance of a People's Court, a citizen, legal person, or other organization may first apply to the administrative organ at the next higher level or to an administrative organ prescribed by laws or regulations for reconsideration; if dissatisfied with the reconsideration decision, he may file a lawsuit with the People's Court; or he may directly file a lawsuit with the People's Court. Where laws or regulations provide that a party shall first apply to an administrative organ for reconsideration and may file a lawsuit with the People's Court only if he is dissatisfied with the reconsideration decision, such provisions shall be followed." Current laws and regulations of China do not contain provisions that a party must first go through the administrative reconsideration procedure before filing an administrative lawsuit regarding a reeducation-through-labor decision. Therefore, the Appellant's direct lawsuit to the People's Court fully complies with legal provisions, and the People's Court should accept the case.

The Appellee Labor Management Committee argued in reply: Pursuant to Article 12(2) of the Interim Measures on Reeducation-through-Labor, which states, "If a person determined to be subject to reeducation-through-labor disagrees with the main facts, the approving authority shall organize a review," and Article 37(2) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, which provides, "Where laws or regulations provide that a party shall first apply to an administrative organ for reconsideration and may file a lawsuit with the People's Court only if he is dissatisfied with the reconsideration decision, such provisions shall be followed," Appellant Bai Guanghua, if dissatisfied with the reeducation-through-labor decision made by the Appellee, should first apply for reconsideration with the approving authority within the prescribed time limit. Since Bai Guanghua directly filed an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court without going through administrative reconsideration, the People's Court should not accept the case. The first-instance ruling found the facts clearly and correctly applied the laws and regulations. The Appellee requests the court of second instance to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original ruling.

The Tianjin High People's Court, upon trial, confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

The focal points of the dispute in the second instance were: 1. Whether the phrase "organized review by the approving authority" in Article 12(2) of the Interim Measures on Reeducation-through-Labor refers to an administrative reconsideration procedure; 2. Whether the People's Court should accept the case when Appellant Bai Guanghua, dissatisfied with the reeducation-through-labor decision made by the Appellee Labor Management Committee, directly filed an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court without going through the administrative reconsideration procedure.

The Tianjin High People's Court held:

I. The phrase "organized review by the approving authority" in Article 12(2) of the Interim Measures on Reeducation-through-Labor does not refer to an administrative reconsideration procedure. According to Article 2 of the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the PRC, a citizen, legal person, or other organization that believes a specific administrative act has infringed its lawful rights and interests may file an application for administrative reconsideration with an administrative organ. So-called administrative reconsideration refers to the activity in which a citizen, legal person, or other organization, believing that a specific administrative act has infringed its lawful rights and interests, files an application with the administrative organ at the next higher level of the organ that made the specific administrative act, or with other statutory organs, in accordance with statutory procedures and conditions, and the said organ reviews the legality and appropriateness of the specific administrative act and renders a reconsideration decision. According to Article 1 of the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the PRC, the purpose of establishing the administrative reconsideration procedure is to prevent and correct illegal or inappropriate specific administrative acts, protect the lawful rights and interests of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations, and ensure and supervise the lawful exercise of powers by administrative organs. It follows that the organ performing the duty of administrative reconsideration should be the administrative organ at the next higher level of the organ that made the specific administrative act, or another statutory organ, and shall not be the organ that made the specific administrative act itself reconsidering its own act. Article 12(2) of the Interim Measures on Reeducation-through-Labor provides: "If a person determined to be subject to reeducation-through-labor disagrees with the main facts, the approving authority shall organize a review." The "approving authority" as referred to herein is exactly the organ that made the reeducation-through-labor decision; the "review" as referred to herein is also different from "reconsideration," and means a reexamination conducted by the original approving authority itself. Therefore, this provision means that the organ that made the reeducation-through-labor decision shall conduct a review by itself, rather than the administrative organ at the next higher level of the organ that made the specific administrative act of reeducation-through-labor, or another statutory organ, conducting administrative reconsideration.

II. Article 37 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC provides: "In the case of an administrative case that falls within the scope of acceptance of a People's Court, a citizen, legal person, or other organization may first apply to the administrative organ at the next higher level or to an administrative organ prescribed by laws or regulations for reconsideration; if dissatisfied with the reconsideration decision, he may file a lawsuit with the People's Court; or he may directly file a lawsuit with the People's Court. Where laws or regulations provide that a party shall first apply to an administrative organ for reconsideration and may file a lawsuit with the People's Court only if he is dissatisfied with the reconsideration decision, such provisions shall be followed." Accordingly, unless laws or regulations explicitly provide that a party shall first apply for administrative reconsideration and may file a lawsuit with the People's Court only if dissatisfied with the reconsideration decision, a citizen, legal person, or other organization who believes that a specific administrative act has infringed its lawful rights and interests may freely choose to apply for administrative reconsideration or directly file an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court. With respect to persons determined to be subject to reeducation-through-labor who are dissatisfied with the reeducation-through-labor decision, current laws and regulations of China do not explicitly provide that they must first apply for reconsideration with the administrative organ at the next higher level of the organ that made the reeducation-through-labor decision, or with another statutory organ, and may file a lawsuit with the People's Court only if dissatisfied with the reconsideration decision; that is, there is no requirement of administrative reconsideration as a prerequisite procedure. Therefore, a person determined to be subject to reeducation-through-labor who is dissatisfied with the reeducation-through-labor decision may either apply for reconsideration with the administrative organ at the next higher level of the organ that made the reeducation-through-labor decision, or with an administrative organ prescribed by laws or regulations, or directly file a lawsuit with the People's Court; if he directly files an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court, the People's Court shall accept it. The first-instance ruling, which determined that Appellant Bai Guanghua's direct filing of an administrative lawsuit with the court without going through the administrative reconsideration procedure was improper, and dismissed the complaint, constituted an error in the application of law and should be corrected.

Accordingly, the Tianjin High People's Court, pursuant to Article 68 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, ruled on October 31, 2005, as follows:

1. The administrative ruling (2005) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 106 of the Tianjin No. 1 Intermediate People's Court is set aside;

2. This case shall be continued to be tried by the Tianjin No. 1 Intermediate People's Court.
